title: Build CrossLatch Rust service and native iOS sharing client
description:
# CrossLatch — implementation handoff

Scaffold a standalone CrossLatch repository and propose its v0 protocol and data model. CrossLatch connects native mobile sharing, agents, and server-side tools through a dynamic registry of typed capabilities. Build the useful standalone system first; later it becomes Oqto’s automation/capability fabric, complementing Oqto apps and offloading expensive work from lean agent sandboxes.

## Requirements

- Rust daemon/API server, launched and managed through a CLI, with a network API for paired clients and a local Unix socket for agents/processes to register capabilities. Use socket ownership and peer identity for local authorization; registration does not imply activation.
- Native iOS and Android clients, paired by QR bootstrap and a secure handshake using per-device keys. Support scoped access and device revocation. Propose the exact authentication scheme, expiry/replay protection, and secure key storage; do not invent cryptography.
- Dynamic capability discovery and a locally cached registry filtered by input MIME type and device permissions. Design the mobile interaction as share to CrossLatch, then choose a compatible action. Verify platform constraints before promising individual native share targets or background delivery.
- Versioned, typed manifests describing identity, title, description, publisher, input/output schemas, accepted MIME types, execution binding, requested permissions, sync/async behavior, and lifetime. One contract should drive discovery, validation, approval UI, and agent/tool descriptions.
- Capability creation starts in draft/pending approval. Show what runs, what resources it touches, network/filesystem access, and persistence. Activation requires explicit approval or an explicit deterministic policy grant. Bind approval to the reviewed revision; relevant changes require review again.
- Enforce deterministic permission checks at registration, activation, invocation, and result access. Optional agent review can explain or flag risks but cannot override policy. Use declared commands and bound arguments rather than interpolated shell strings. Distinguish process-scoped exposure from persistent installation as a proposed lifecycle.
- Support immediate responses and asynchronous jobs using the same invocation model. Start with SQLite-backed jobs and events, artifact/result references, status/error tracking, bounded worker concurrency, and a simple documented restart/retry policy. Define idempotency and cancellation semantics without promising exactly-once execution.
- Mobile users can submit and leave, receive completion/failure notifications, then retrieve text or files in the client. Persist results independently of notification delivery. Propose reconnect/event replay and platform push integration; a live connection alone must not be treated as reliable background notification delivery.
- Agents are both publishers and consumers through discover/describe/invoke primitives. MCP is an adapter over the core model. Provide a language-neutral local protocol and an agent registration skill; JSON/JSON-lines is a candidate, not a settled transport choice.

## Example capabilities

1. Audio → transcription text.
2. Shared text, URL, or file → prompt an existing agent session, such as pi.
3. Prompt → ComfyUI image-generation job → notification and image retrieval/save.
4. Media → FFmpeg processing job → downloadable output.

## First implementation request

Propose the protocol operations, envelopes, errors, event semantics, and SQLite entities: devices, publishers, capability revisions, approvals/grants, invocations/jobs, job events, and artifacts. Specify ownership, relationships, and capability/job state transitions. Clearly separate settled requirements from proposed defaults and open decisions.

Then scaffold the Rust workspace with clear core, daemon, CLI, persistence, executor, and adapter boundaries; migrations; example manifests; protocol documentation; and native client starter directories. Implement one working vertical slice: register a harmless capability locally → approve it → discover/invoke through an authenticated client → persist the job → retrieve its result. Test permission denial, revocation, unapproved revisions, and restart recovery. Keep retries and scheduling minimal initially; defer distributed queues and full Oqto integration.

## Suggested skills

Use domain-modeling and codebase-design for terminology and boundaries; ripwire-before-you-build when an existing repository is available. Use platform documentation to validate native sharing, pairing, and notification decisions.

Source: ChatGPT conversation “Share Sheet Idea”, 6aa50764-ac5c-83ed-a593-1d728c5f3603. This handoff captures concept decisions; no repository implementation was established in that discussion.


Current execution request (supersedes handoff-only wording): govnr is the builder/orchestrator; xlatch is the standalone owning repository. File implementation in this repository's trx and build the Rust CLI/API server and native iOS app now. Reuse the existing Rust template. An iPhone is connected to this Mac and registered with Xcode; produce a signed installable build and install for testing if available. Android stays in the longer-term concept but is not part of this immediate implementation request. Preserve the existing uncommitted scaffold. Do not claim unimplemented integrations or notification delivery. Deliver a tested useful first version, with remaining expansion work explicitly tracked.

title: Define v0 capability protocol and durable data model
description: Formalize typed manifests, publisher/device identities, revision-bound approval and grants, job lifecycle, ownership and artifact contracts. Update glossary and a concise protocol document. Include examples for transcription, agent-session prompts, ComfyUI, and FFmpeg. MCP adapts core discovery/describe/invoke. Distinguish v0 implementation from later extensions.

title: Build Rust daemon and CLI with local registration and approval
description: Extend xlatch-core/cli/api. Implement Unix-socket registration, deterministic authorization, draft/pending approval and activation, manifest validation and revision binding, configurable service startup. Preserve binary-to-core dependency direction. Demonstrate registration, rejection before approval, activation, and discovery.

title: Add secure QR pairing and per-device API access
description: Implement QR bootstrap with expiring single-use enrollment, per-device cryptographic keys, revocation, scoped permissions, secure transport and authenticated requests. Use established cryptography. Test replay/expiry, invalid identity, revocation, and unauthorized capability/result access. Agree exact interoperable wire contract with the iOS client.

title: Persist jobs and results in SQLite with execution and events
description: Implement sync/async invocation, SQLite jobs/events/artifact references, bounded workers, safe parameter binding and input/output validation. Define retry/idempotency/cancellation/restart semantics. Include a harmless end-to-end capability and useful adapter examples. Test failures and restart recovery; no exactly-once promises. Results remain available when notifications fail.

title: Build native iOS app and dynamic share extension
description: Build SwiftUI iOS app plus share extension, QR enrollment, Keychain device keys, cached permission-filtered registry, compatible input selection, submission, job/status/result UI and result sharing/save. Handle disconnected state and errors. Support a reliable foreground/reconnect event path; label actual background notification limitations and track push work explicitly. Verify on simulator and build for the registered physical iPhone.

title: Validate integrated CLI/API/iOS flow and install iPhone test build
description: Run proportional Rust tests and formatter, native build/tests, and end-to-end approved invocation. Verify negative authorization paths and recovery. Use existing Xcode signing/device setup without overwriting unrelated credentials. Install test app on the connected iPhone if signing permits. Provide tested workflow and honest limitations in docs/implementation-report.md; keep other issues open until acceptance is met.

Current local socket/MCP are trusted OS-operator adapters and must not be mounted into untrusted Apps. Do not touch govnr.

Keep deterministic activation/grants authoritative; changing content must not inherit approval.

description: Protocol examples are documented; only echo and FFmpeg are runnable here. Build fixed, reviewed JSON adapters for configured transcription endpoint, existing authorized agent session, and selected ComfyUI workflow. Keep credentials out of manifests/logs, restrict endpoint/session/workflow choices, and validate live integration before advertising availability.

title: Add streaming artifact storage and result retention
description: Current protocol uses inline Base64 artifacts (4 MiB native file limit, 8 MiB envelope, 6 MiB serialized result). Add owned upload/download resources, integrity checks, quotas, cleanup/retention, pagination and result references. Preserve result availability independently from notifications.

title: Implement Windows local control transport and validate release matrix
description: Current v0 local authority uses Unix socket permissions and peer uid. Existing template Windows release target is not a supported v0 build. Add a Windows named-pipe or equivalent transport with explicit OS identity/ACL semantics and equivalent tests before claiming Windows support or releasing that target.

title: Protect enrollment with phone-signed biometric approval
description: Implement trusted first-approver bootstrap and pending additional-device enrollment. Define resource ownership and broker enforcement: resources already accessible to agent are not protected by approval. Test as unprivileged agent attempts DB/binary/policy tampering and API bypass. Administrator/root compromise is outside this boundary. Installation requires explicit privileged OS setup; do not modify host accounts until concrete installer reviewed.
